> 曲則全，枉則直，窪則盈，敝則新，少則得，多則惑.

Six lines, all the same shape: a disadvantage that produces an advantage, or the reverse.

Read fast, they are aphorisms about getting along. Read slowly, there is a harder sentence underneath: these six are not six strategies. They are six cross-sections of one law.

## The law, not the tactics

曲 is a bent thing — curved, therefore whole; a thing that insists on being straight breaks. 枉 is crooked, and it is by yielding that it becomes straight again. 窪 is low ground, and low ground fills. 敝 is worn, and worn things renew. 少 is few, and few obtains. 多 is many, and many confuses.

Each pair describes the same mechanism from a different position: what is full cannot receive, what is straightened by force snaps, what is low collects.

If they were tactics, they would be instructions about how to behave. As a law, they are statements about how things behave, and behavior instructions follow only if you want to stay inside the law.

## 抱一為天下式

> 是以聖人抱一為天下式.

一 is the one — not a number, but the undivided. 抱 is to hold, to embrace. 式 is the pattern, the mold, the standard.

The sage holds the undivided as the standard for the world. Which is the answer to the six lines: you don't manage six separate trade-offs. You hold the one thing that keeps the trade-offs from being decisions at all.

## 四不自

> 不自見，故明；不自是，故彰；不自伐，故有功；不自矜，故長.

Four negations, four results.

- 不自見 — not parading the self: therefore clear.
- 不自是 — not asserting that one is right: therefore evident.
- 不自伐 — not claiming credit: therefore the work registers.
- 不自矜 — not exalting oneself: therefore lasting.

Each result is not a reward for modesty. It is what becomes possible when a specific obstruction is removed. Clarity is obstructed by parading. Being seen is obstructed by insisting on being right. Credit is obstructed by grabbing it. Duration is obstructed by self-inflation.

## 夫唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭

Only because there is no contest can no one contest with him.

The line is not a strategy for winning by appearing not to compete. It is the observation that a person who has not entered the contest has no position for anyone to attack. There is nothing to displace.

## 誠全而歸之

The last four characters are where the chapter gets regularly misread, as "bend and you will be preserved; yield and you will profit."

歸 is not 得. 歸 is to return home.

So the claim is: 曲則全 is not a trade — sacrifice a little shape now, collect wholeness later. It says: what is bent returns to the whole it came from. The wholeness is not a payment; it is the place.

Read as exchange, the chapter teaches calculated humility, which curdles fast. Read as return, it says the bent thing is not broken — it is on its way back.

## The test

Pick one place where you are holding a straight line by force — a position, a self-description, an argument you will not soften. Ask what it would look like if the shape were allowed to bend. The usual answer is that nothing is lost except the maintenance.
